story_review.one_viewing_summary: Planned chain read from the board and callable code, not observed pixels. In a rainy San Antonio yard with no station in it, brown water tops a limestone curb, climbs a chain link post to an orange ankle mark and reaches rain boots on the porch step. The phone on the rail stays dark, then a Flash Flood Warning banner lands late. A tagged prototype station is revealed at a curb. Its solar panel fills the battery bar, and a dashed link toward a far cell tower stops short under a 'No cell tower needed' tag. The view climbs four lenses at four heights, water crosses the second lens and it lights, then four labelled weather lamps come on. In the opened housing, readings run along traces into a TinyML chip. The view pushes in as the chip lights an amber risk lamp, 'Judged on the station' pins, and a far dashed central server stays dark with nothing joining them. Radio rings leave the antenna, pass a half-mile tag down a bungalow street and reach a hub mast in open country as its lamp lights and a five-mile tag pins. At the hub desk, station dots arrive and 'A second, larger model' pins. Overhead, flood paths spread and higher-risk zones outline for emergency responders. A validation card fills to 98.82% under 'Initial assessments after training', and a Field result card takes a None reported stamp. A paper map on a curbside fence is searched and shows no pin. At the empty curb a dashed station outline draws itself where one could stand, a dashed goal pin hovers, and 'Deployment goal' pins.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The opening question asks whether a station can judge rising street water with no power line or tower. The middle answers it as a design: sun charge, four lenses, a local chip judgment with no server, and radio to a hub map for responders. s7 and s8 give the honest limit of a validation figure only, no field result and no named installation. The close shows that limit as a picture: an empty curb, an uninstalled dashed outline and a goal pin that has not landed. It answers 'what happens next' without inventing a deployment or outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: s1 to s2. The household yard, deliberately with no station, cuts to a prototype standing at a different curb in shallow water. The transition calls this 'the same brown flood water', so the viewer must take s2 as a design illustration rather than this street. The 'Prototype flood station' tag and the 'Illustration of the prototype' chip carry that meaning, and the chip shows only after the county locator ends at 8.1 s. Before that the chip reads 'Illustration. Map marks the county'.
